# registry


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

AnswerUI provides built-in components through its shared stylesheet and
JavaScript assets. Python constructors render their marked HTML. This
registry holds application CSS and event handlers, attaches custom rules
to constructors, and assembles those additions for each page. Built-in
CSS remains in the shared assets instead of being copied into registry
entries.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import Label, Input, Button, to_xml
from fastcore.test import *
```

## Rules

Both styling and behavior pair a CSS selector with an action: CSS
declarations for styling, or an event name and JavaScript handler for
behavior. A `Rule` stores both CSS text and behavior records under a
[cascade layer](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer)
because each page loads one combined stylesheet and one combined script.

The layer list is fixed and ordered. For normal declarations, each layer
overrides earlier layers regardless of specificity. You can restyle a
built-in component from the `app` layer without changing its definition.
Component and base CSS do not use `!important` because `!important`
reverses cascade-layer order (only the hidden-state classes in
`utilities` use it).

Behaviors are passed as a dict from `(selector, event)` keys to
JavaScript handler bodies. Each handler runs with `el` bound to the
matched element and `e` to the event. For an event that doesn’t bubble,
such as `toggle`, add a truthy third item to the key to attach the
handler in the capture phase. When a rule has a root selector `sel`,
`_behaviors` replaces each `&` in its behavior selectors with `:is(sel)`
(raising `ValueError` if `sel` is missing).

A rule’s key is a name, or `owner.name` when the rule belongs to a
hyperelement. `Rule` checks the layer, expands the behaviors, and
derives `owner` and `name` from the key. For a variant rule, the variant
attribute is stored in `variant`:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Rule

``` python
def Rule(
    key, # Registry key: a name, or `owner.name` for a hyperelement's rule
    css:str='', # Complete CSS, or a no-argument function returning it
    *, on:NoneType=None, # Mapping of (selector, event[, capture]) to JavaScript handler bodies
    sel:NoneType=None, # Root selector substituted for `&` in behaviors
    layer:str='app', # One of LAYERS
    doc:str='', # Description of the rule
    variant:NoneType=None, # Attribute selecting a declared variant
):
```

*A named CSS and behavior definition in a cascade layer*

`Registry.rule` takes CSS first and an optional name second. Without a
name, it hashes the CSS, selector, expanded behaviors and layer into a
deterministic key. Identical registrations share one entry, including
behavior-only rules. Pass an explicit name when `css` is callable, or
when later edits should replace the previous rule rather than add
another. A component’s rule uses `owner.name` as its key.

Rules are stored in `Registry.rules`. Registering an existing key
updates that `Rule` object in place, preserving both existing references
and its position in the stylesheet. Registering or removing a rule
increments `version`, which `Registry.assets` checks before rebuilding
the stylesheet and script. Each entry of `layers` is a live `RuleView`
of the rules in that layer:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Registry

``` python
def Registry():
```

*Named rules and hyperelements, from which a page’s stylesheet and
script are built*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### RuleView

``` python
def RuleView(
    registry, *, layer:NoneType=None, owner:NoneType=None
):
```

*A live, read-only view of one layer or one hyperelement’s rules*

The simplest rule is bare CSS with no constructor, such as a centered
page column. Its layer defaults to `app`. Registering the same name
again returns the existing entry:

``` python
page_css = 'main { max-width: 65ch; margin-inline: auto; padding: 1rem; }'
page_rule = reg.rule(page_css, 'app-page', doc='A centered single-column page.')
test_eq(page_rule.css, page_css)
test_is(reg.rule(page_css, 'app-page', doc='A centered single-column page.'), page_rule)
page_rule
```

    app-page [app]: A centered single-column page.

A standalone behavior works the same way. Here we add a `select-all`
attribute that selects an input’s text on focus. Passing
`sel='input[select-all]'` sets the root selector that `&` expands to in
the handler key. The rule stores the expanded behavior record:

``` python
select_all = reg.rule(name='select-all', sel='input[select-all]', on={('&', 'focusin'): r"el.select()"},
    doc='Select the input text when it receives focus.')
select_all.on
```

    [{'sel': ':is(input[select-all])',
      'ev': 'focusin',
      'js': 'el.select()',
      'cap': False}]

``` python
with expect_fail(ValueError): reg.rule('a { color: teal; }', layer='appp')
with expect_fail(ValueError): reg.rule(name='paste', on={('&', 'click'): ''})
```

Displaying `reg` lists each rule that belongs to no component, such as
`app-page` and `select-all`:

``` python
reg
```

Registry(2 rules, 0 elements)

Layers: - `reset`: 0 rules - `tokens`: 0 rules - `base`: 0 rules -
`layout`: 0 rules - `components`: 0 rules - `app`: 2 rules -
`utilities`: 0 rules

Elements: none

Rules of no element: - `app-page` (app): A centered single-column

focus.

## Building the stylesheet

`build_css` starts with the shared `styles.css`, whose opening `@layer`
statement declares the layer order. Registered rules follow as one
`@layer` block per layer in registration order, each preceded by a
comment naming its key. Application rules default to `app`, after the
built-in `components` layer. For CSS that depends on later
registrations, pass a zero-argument callable that `build_css` evaluates
during assembly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Registry.build_css

``` python
def build_css():
```

*The shared foundation followed by registered CSS in cascade-layer
order*

``` python
reg.layers['app']
```

    app-page [app]: A centered single-column page.
    select-all [app] input[select-all]: Select the input text when it receives focus.

## Hyperelements

A component pairs a constructor (a standard FastTag or a Python function
combining multiple tags) with registered rules. Calling a `Hyperelement`
invokes that constructor. Its `sel` attribute holds the root selector.
Its `rules` attribute is a live `RuleView` of the component’s rules:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Hyperelement

``` python
def Hyperelement(
    registry, name, fn, sel, doc:str='', generated:bool=False
):
```

*A callable constructor linked to its registered rules and behaviors*

Use `Hyperelement.rule` to add CSS nested under the root selector, or
`Hyperelement.variant` to add an attribute variant nested under
`:is(sel)[name]`. Both register their rule with the hyperelement as its
owner. Calling `variant` also stores the attribute name on the rule
(`base` is reserved for the constructor’s own rule):

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Hyperelement.variant

``` python
def variant(
    name, # Attribute selecting the variant; also its local rule name
    css:str='', # CSS declarations and nested rules, scoped to the variant
    *, on:NoneType=None, # Mapping of (selector, event[, capture]) to handler bodies; `&` is the variant selector
    layer:str='app', # One of LAYERS
    doc:str='', # Description shown with the variant
):
```

*Declare an attribute variant without changing the constructor*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Hyperelement.rule

``` python
def rule(
    name, # Local rule name; registering it again replaces that rule
    css:str='', # CSS declarations and nested rules, scoped to the root selector
    *, on:NoneType=None, # Mapping of (selector, event[, capture]) to handler bodies; `&` is the root selector
    layer:str='app', # One of LAYERS
    doc:str='', # Description of the customization
):
```

*Register CSS and behaviors scoped to this hyperelement*

`hypelt` registers a component from a FastHTML tag name or a handwritten
constructor and nests `css` under its root selector as the `base` rule,
just like `Hyperelement.rule`. Write declarations for the root, nested
selectors for children, and `&` for states or pseudo-elements on the
root. Pass a callable with no parameters when `css` depends on later
registrations. Put global rules such as `@keyframes` in `reg.rule`,
which accepts complete CSS without wrapping and uses its `sel` parameter
for behaviors only. The module-level `hypelt` is bound to `reg`:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Registry.hypelt

``` python
def hypelt(
    name:NoneType=None, # FastHTML tag name or a constructor; omit to use as a decorator
    *, sel:NoneType=None, # Root selector; required for a handwritten constructor
    css:str='', # CSS declarations and nested rules, or a no-argument function returning them
    on:NoneType=None, # Mapping of (selector, event[, capture]) to JavaScript handler bodies
    layer:str='app', # One of LAYERS; built-ins use components, layout, or base
    doc:NoneType=None, # Description; defaults to a handwritten constructor's docstring
):
```

*Register a constructor and its base rule, returning a callable
hyperelement*

As an example component, let’s build a dismissible notice box with a
close button. Because HTML has no built-in notice element, we use the
custom tag `notice-box`. Clicking any child with the `dismiss` attribute
removes the notice:

``` python
notice_css = r"""
display: block;
padding: .75rem 1rem;
background: #f4f4f6;
border: 1px solid #ccc;
border-radius: 8px;
"""
NoticeBox = hypelt('NoticeBox', css=notice_css, on={('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"el.closest('notice-box').remove()"},
    layer='components', doc='A dismissible notice.')
to_xml(NoticeBox('Changes saved.', Button('Dismiss', dismiss=True)))
```

    '<notice-box>Changes saved.<button dismiss>Dismiss</button></notice-box>'

For a string name such as `'NoticeBox'`, `hypelt` looks up the
constructor on `fasthtml.components` and calls it with no arguments to
get the root selector (`notice-box`). `NoticeBox.rules` and `reg.rules`
hold the same `Rule` object:

``` python
test_eq(NoticeBox().tag, NoticeBox.sel)
assert NoticeBox.rules['base'] is reg.rules['NoticeBox.base']
assert NoticeBox.rules['base'].compiled_css.startswith('notice-box {')
NoticeBox
```

### `NoticeBox(*children, **attrs)`

A dismissible notice.

Root selector: `notice-box`.

Rules: - `base` (components)

The second case is a handwritten constructor, such as a labelled field
that wraps an `input` inside its `label` to associate them without an
`id`. Because `Field` requires a `label` argument, `hypelt` can’t call
it with no arguments to infer a root selector. Instead we mark the
`label` with a `field` attribute and pass `sel='label[field]'` using the
decorator form:

``` python
field_css = r"""
display: grid;
gap: .5rem;
"""

@hypelt(sel='label[field]', css=field_css)
def Field(label, **attrs):
    "A labelled input"
    return Label(label, Input(**attrs), field=True)

to_xml(Field('Email', name='email', type='email'))
```

    '<label field>Email  <input name="email" type="email">\n</label>'

## Customization

There are two ways to change a component’s styling or behavior. To
override a component without altering its `base` rule, register separate
rules in the `app` layer. To redefine it, call `hypelt` again with the
same name to replace its constructor and `base` rule in place.

### Overrides

Say a developer wants rounder notices in their application.
`NoticeBox.rule` registers a named rule in the `app` layer by default,
where it overrides the component’s CSS in the `components` layer:

``` python
NoticeBox.rule('corners', 'border-radius: 1rem;', doc='Rounder notices in this application.')
```

    NoticeBox.corners [app] notice-box: Rounder notices in this application.

To select a style with an attribute, declare it with `variant`. Its
description then appears in the hyperelement’s documentation while the
existing constructor accepts the attribute:

``` python
NoticeBox.variant('quiet', 'background: transparent; border-color: transparent;', doc='An unfilled notice without a visible border.')
```

    NoticeBox.quiet [app] :is(notice-box)[quiet]: An unfilled notice without a visible border.

``` python
test_eq(list(NoticeBox.variants), ['quiet'])
to_xml(NoticeBox('Saved quietly.', quiet=True))
```

    '<notice-box quiet>Saved quietly.</notice-box>'

To change a component only within part of a page, register an
application rule scoped to that container. Here `reg.rule` registers
`editor-notices` to square the corners of every `notice-box` inside an
`[editor]` element, with an explicit name for later replacement. Because
this rule is not registered on `NoticeBox`, it leaves the component’s
definition untouched and appears in `reg.layers['app']` rather than
`NoticeBox.rules`:

``` python
reg.rule('[editor] notice-box { border-radius: 0; }', 'editor-notices', doc='Square notices inside the editor.')
reg.layers['app']
```

    app-page [app]: A centered single-column page.
    select-all [app] input[select-all]: Select the input text when it receives focus.
    Field.base [app] label[field]: A labelled input
    NoticeBox.corners [app] notice-box: Rounder notices in this application.
    NoticeBox.quiet [app] :is(notice-box)[quiet]: An unfilled notice without a visible border.
    editor-notices [app]: Square notices inside the editor.

### Redefinitions

Calling `hypelt` again with the same name updates the hyperelement’s
constructor and `base` rule in place, preserving existing references,
application rules, and declared variants. Omitted `css` or `on`
arguments are cleared rather than merged because the new call replaces
the entire `base` rule. `hypelt` raises `ValueError` if `sel` changes
because existing rules and variants are nested under the original root
selector. Omitting `on` here makes `NoticeBox` persistent:

``` python
original, base = NoticeBox, NoticeBox.rules['base']
NoticeBox = hypelt('NoticeBox', css=lambda: notice_css.replace('8px', '12px'), layer='components', doc='A persistent notice.')
test_is(NoticeBox, original)
test_is(NoticeBox.rules['base'], base)
assert '12px' in base.compiled_css
assert 'corners' in NoticeBox.rules and 'quiet' in NoticeBox.variants
with expect_fail(ValueError): hypelt('NoticeBox', sel='notice-box[persistent]', css=notice_css, layer='components')
NoticeBox
```

### `NoticeBox(*children, **attrs)`

A persistent notice.

Root selector: `notice-box`.

Declared variants: - `quiet`: An unfilled notice without a visible
border.

Rules: - `base` (components) - `corners` (app): Rounder notices in this
application.

The base rule now has no behaviors. To remove the application override,
pass its full key to `reg.remove`. A layer view taken earlier no longer
lists it:

``` python
test_eq(NoticeBox.behaviors, [])
app_rules = reg.layers['app']
v = reg.version
reg.remove('NoticeBox.corners')
```

    NoticeBox.corners [app] notice-box: Rounder notices in this application.

``` python
assert 'NoticeBox.corners' not in app_rules
test_eq(reg.version, v+1)
app_rules
```

    app-page [app]: A centered single-column page.
    select-all [app] input[select-all]: Select the input text when it receives focus.
    Field.base [app] label[field]: A labelled input
    NoticeBox.quiet [app] :is(notice-box)[quiet]: An unfilled notice without a visible border.
    editor-notices [app]: Square notices inside the editor.
